<reason>B established a concrete benefit: discovering disqualifying conditions before wasting comparison and coordination effort. It directly answered both pressure questions and explained how the requirement permits flexible presentation. A raised plausible compliance and defensive-disclosure concerns, but overstated their certainty and never established that existing laws or host incentives reliably eliminate the disclosure gap. B also correctly distinguished an outcome requirement from a duplicative statute. Its case survived the exchange more convincingly.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B showed that earlier access and focused checkout confirmation are complements, not alternatives. This undercut A’s attention objection, while B’s closing explicitly corrected A’s claim that the motion mandates two disclosure touchpoints.</best_rebuttal>
